title: Sambal Yojana MP: Sambal Card, Benefits, Registration
meta_description: Sambal Yojana MP gives unorganised workers Rs 4 lakh accident cover, Rs 2 lakh on death, maternity Rs 16,000 and funeral Rs 5,000. Register at sambal.mp.gov.in.

hero.one_liner: Sambal Yojana is MP's social security cover for unorganised workers. Sambal Card, Rs 4 lakh accident cover, maternity, registration, and claims explained.

what_is_it: Mukhyamantri Jan Kalyan (Sambal) Yojana is the Madhya Pradesh government's social security umbrella for unorganised sector workers. Any MP resident aged 18 to 60 who works in the informal economy and holds a BPL card can enrol. Registration is free and is done at sambal.mp.gov.in using a Samagra ID. After enrolment, the worker receives a Sambal Card that activates cover for accidental death (Rs 4 lakh), natural death (Rs 2 lakh), disability, funeral aid, maternity assistance of Rs 16,000, free electricity up to 200 units per month, and education support for children through the Medhavi Kalyan scheme. All cash benefits are paid via Direct Benefit Transfer to the worker's registered bank account.

Mukhyamantri Jan Kalyan (Sambal) Yojana was launched in 2018 by the Shivraj Singh Chouhan government in Madhya Pradesh as a single-window social security system for the state's vast unorganised workforce. The scheme replaced a fragmented set of earlier labour welfare programmes and consolidated them under one registration, one card and one portal at sambal.mp.gov.in.

eligibility.label: Work
eligibility.value: Employed in the unorganised sector, not under ESIC or EPF.

eligibility.label: Income
eligibility.value: Annual family income below Rs 2.5 lakh (BPL card holders included). Confirm the current ceiling on the portal.

eligibility.label: Land
eligibility.value: Should not own more than one hectare of irrigated agricultural land.

eligibility.value: A valid Samagra ID is mandatory before registration.

eligibility_filters.notes: MP resident unorganised worker, age 18-60, BPL or family income below Rs 2.5 lakh, not under ESIC/EPF, not owning more than one hectare irrigated land. Samagra ID mandatory.

how_to_apply.title: Get a Samagra ID first
how_to_apply.description: Samagra ID is the gateway to Sambal registration and cannot be skipped. If your family is not yet on the Samagra portal, visit samagra.gov.in or your nearest Gram Panchayat office to enrol and receive a 9-digit family ID and a separate individual member ID for each person in the household.

how_to_apply.title: Open the Sambal portal and start registration
how_to_apply.description: Go to sambal.mp.gov.in and click on 'Panjeeyan hetu aavedan kare' (Apply for Registration). The portal is also accessible via sambal.mponline.gov.in, which is operated by MPOnline and functions identically to the main portal for the purpose of registration and document upload.

how_to_apply.title: Enter Samagra ID and verify pre-filled details
how_to_apply.description: Type your 9-digit Samagra family ID along with your individual member ID. The system auto-fills your name, address, date of birth, and Aadhaar number from the Samagra database, so verify each field carefully before proceeding, as errors here will delay Panchayat verification and card issuance.

how_to_apply.title: Select occupation and enter bank account details
how_to_apply.description: Choose your occupation from the dropdown covering construction labourer, domestic help, street vendor, daily wage worker, weaver, rickshaw puller, agricultural labourer and other informal trades. Enter your bank account number, IFSC code and nominee name with relationship, so that all DBT payments can be directed correctly.

how_to_apply.title: Upload documents and submit the application
how_to_apply.description: Scan and upload your Aadhaar card, BPL ration card, bank passbook showing account number and IFSC, and one passport-size photograph in the required format. After clicking submit, note the application reference number displayed on the confirmation screen for future status tracking.

how_to_apply.title: Panchayat verification and Sambal Card receipt
how_to_apply.description: The submitted application is forwarded to your Gram Panchayat Secretary or Ward Officer for field verification, which typically takes 15 to 30 days. After approval, the Sambal Card is generated and can be downloaded as a PDF from sambal.mp.gov.in or collected as a printed copy from the Panchayat office.

ministry: Labour Department, Government of Madhya Pradesh

extra_sections.heading: What Is Sambal Yojana MP
content: Between 2018 and 2020, the Congress government briefly renamed the scheme Naya Savera Yojana with some structural changes. After BJP returned to power in March 2020, the scheme was immediately restored to its original Sambal name and expanded as Sambal 2.0 with higher benefit amounts and a broader list of eligible worker categories.

extra_sections.heading: Sambal Yojana MP: Key Benefit Amounts
Who Runs Sambal and Who It Covers
content: The implementing body is the Madhya Pradesh Unorganized Urban and Rural Workers Welfare Board, operating under the state Labour Department and headquartered at 82 Harshvardhan Nagar in Bhopal. The Board oversees registration, Sambal Card issuance, claim processing and grievance resolution across all 52 districts of Madhya Pradesh.

Unorganised workers covered under the scheme include construction labourers, domestic workers, street vendors, rickshaw and auto-rickshaw pullers, daily wage earners, weavers, cobblers, stone quarry workers, small and marginal agricultural labourers, fisherfolk, and others in informal trades. Small farmers who do not file income tax returns and work their own land are also eligible.

extra_sections.heading: Eligibility Conditions in Detail
content: The eligibility conditions are precise and non-negotiable: the applicant must be a permanent resident of Madhya Pradesh, aged 18 to 60 years, hold a BPL ration card, work in the unorganised sector, and must not be a beneficiary of ESIC or EPF. Income tax payers and those with organised-sector employment contracts are excluded from the scheme.

Samagra ID is the most critical requirement for registration because the Sambal portal does not maintain its own separate citizen database. All personal data, including name, date of birth, address and Aadhaar number, is pulled from the state's Samagra portal, which serves as the universal beneficiary registry for every social security scheme in Madhya Pradesh.

extra_sections.heading: Who qualifies
qualify: Permanent resident of Madhya Pradesh aged 18 to 60
Works in the unorganised sector (labour, domestic, vendor, farmer, etc.)
Holds a BPL card or family income below Rs 2.5 lakh
Gig and platform workers, now included under Sambal
disqualify: Owns more than one hectare of irrigated land
No Samagra ID (must create one first)

extra_sections.heading: Special Cases: Migrants, CSCs and Urban Workers
content: For the first pregnancy, Rs 3,000 is routed through the Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana as its first and second installments, with the remaining Rs 13,000 released via the state Prasuti Sahayata scheme. From the second child onwards, the full Rs 16,000 is channelled entirely through the state scheme without any split with the central programme.

To access education support, the student applies at the start of each academic year by logging into medhavikalyan.mp.gov.in and linking the parent's Sambal registration number. The college fee demand is verified and the eligible fee amount is credited directly to the institution's account or the student's bank account depending on the sub-scheme category.

extra_sections.title: New in 2026: Gig Workers and Ayushman Cover
extra_sections.content:
Gig and platform workers have now been brought under Sambal and get the same benefits as traditional workers, with registration underway.

Sambal enrolees also get priority inclusion in Ayushman Bharat, giving up to Rs 5 lakh a year in cashless treatment, over and above Sambal's own cash benefits.

extra_sections.heading: The Sambal Card and Re-registration
content: The Sambal Card issued after registration is both a physical document and a portal-linked digital record. It carries the worker's registration number, Samagra ID, occupation, nominee details and bank account, and must be produced along with Aadhaar at the time of any benefit claim or when approaching any government office for scheme-related assistance.

Workers who enrolled under the pre-2018 Sambal scheme or the Naya Savera Yojana were required to re-register under Sambal 2.0 on the same portal. Re-registration uses the same process as a fresh application but requires the old registration number, which the system uses to migrate the existing beneficiary record rather than creating a duplicate entry.

extra_sections.heading: How to Register for the Sambal Card

steps.title: Get a Samagra ID
steps.desc: Samagra ID is mandatory and cannot be skipped. Create one at samagra.gov.in or your Gram Panchayat if your family is not already listed.

steps.title: Open the Sambal portal
steps.desc: Go to sambal.mp.gov.in, click Panjeeyan hetu aavedan kare, and enter your Samagra family and member ID to auto-fill your details.

steps.title: Add occupation and bank details
steps.desc: Select your occupation, enter bank account, IFSC, and nominee, then upload Aadhaar, BPL card, passbook, and photo.

steps.title: Panchayat verification
steps.desc: The application goes to your Panchayat Secretary or Ward Officer for field verification, usually 15 to 30 days, after which the Sambal Card is generated.

items.title: Construction and labour
items.sub: Construction labourers form the single largest group. Occupation can be proved with a contractor certificate, Panchayat-countersigned self-declaration, or MGNREGA job card.

items.title: Informal trades
items.sub: Domestic workers, street vendors, rickshaw pullers, weavers, cobblers, quarry workers, fisherfolk, and daily wage earners are all eligible.

items.title: Women workers
items.sub: Women in domestic work, beedi rolling, agarbatti making, and farm labour can register as the primary beneficiary if listed as head of household in Samagra.

items.title: Small farmers
items.sub: Small and marginal farmers who do not file income tax and work their own land qualify, subject to the one-hectare irrigated-land limit.

extra_sections.heading: The Accidental and Natural Death Benefits
content: The accidental death benefit of Rs 4,00,000 is the highest cash payout under the scheme and is transferred via DBT directly to the registered nominee's bank account. The claim must be filed within 45 days of the accident along with the FIR copy, post-mortem report, death certificate and the worker's Sambal Card number.

Natural or general death of a registered worker triggers a separate family benefit of Rs 2,00,000, regardless of whether the death was due to illness, old age, or any other non-accidental cause. The worker's Sambal registration must have been active, meaning not suspended or expired, at the time of death for the claim to be valid.

extra_sections.title: The Accidental Death Cover
extra_sections.desc:
The accidental death benefit is the highest payout, transferred by DBT to the registered nominee.

The claim must be filed within 45 days of the accident with the FIR, post-mortem report, death certificate, and Sambal Card number.

extra_sections.heading: How Death and Disability Claims Are Filed
content: The death benefit claim is filed at the Gram Panchayat or Nagar Palika office with the death certificate, Sambal Card, Aadhaar of the deceased, and the nominee's bank details. The claim then goes to the Block Officer for verification and reaches the District Collector's office for sanction before the DBT is released.

Permanent disability from an accident qualifies the registered worker for Rs 2,00,000, while partial permanent disability, where only partial function of a limb or sense is lost, carries Rs 1,00,000. A disability certificate from a recognised government hospital specifying the nature and degree of disability is the primary document required to process either claim.

items.title: Accidental death (₹4L)
items.sub: FIR copy, post-mortem report, death certificate, Sambal Card number, nominee bank details. File within 45 days.

items.title: Natural death (₹2L)
items.sub: Death certificate, Sambal Card, Aadhaar of the deceased, nominee bank details. Registration must have been active at the time of death.

items.title: Disability (₹2L / ₹1L)
items.sub: Disability certificate from a recognised government hospital specifying nature and degree of disability.

items.title: Funeral aid (₹5,000)
items.sub: Death certificate and Sambal Card at the Gram Panchayat. Released within about 48 hours as immediate relief.

extra_sections.heading: Funeral and Maternity Support
content: Funeral assistance of Rs 5,000 is the scheme's fastest benefit and is processed with priority as immediate relief for antyeshti (last rites) expenses. Any family member, relative or even a community representative can file the claim at the Gram Panchayat or Ward office with the death certificate and the worker's Sambal Card, and the amount is typically released within 48 hours.

The maternity benefit under Sambal works through a linked programme called Mukhyamantri Shramik Seva Prasuti Sahayata Yojna. Registered women workers in the unorganised sector receive total maternity support of Rs 16,000 per pregnancy, paid in installments before and after delivery through DBT to the woman's bank account.

extra_sections.title: How the Rs 16,000 Maternity Benefit Works
extra_sections.content:
Registered women workers get Rs 16,000 per pregnancy through the linked Prasuti Sahayata scheme, paid in installments by DBT.

For the first pregnancy, Rs 3,000 routes through PM Matru Vandana and Rs 13,000 through the state scheme. From the second child, the full Rs 16,000 comes through the state scheme.

extra_sections.heading: Maternity: Timing and Documents
content: Applications for maternity assistance must be submitted at the nearest public health centre (PHC) or Block Family Welfare Department office at least six weeks before the expected delivery date. Women who cannot meet this window for any reason can still file the claim immediately after delivery and will not face rejection on account of late submission alone.

Documents required for a maternity claim include the Aadhaar card, Sambal Card, pregnancy confirmation certificate from a government hospital or accredited health provider, bank passbook, a passport-size photo, and post-delivery hospital documents after the child is born. The husband of the registered woman worker also receives 15 days of paid paternity support under the scheme's linked provision.

extra_sections.text: Meri patni ko prasav ke time Sambal ke through 16,000 rupaye mile. Main ek chowkidar hoon aur yeh paisa hamare liye bahut bada sahara tha. Humne pehle suna tha lekin tab tak nahi mana jab tak humara khud ka paisa bank mein aaya.

extra_sections.heading: Education, Electricity and Farm Benefits
content: Education support for children of Sambal workers is delivered through the Mukhyamantri Medhavi Vidyarthi Kalyan Yojana at medhavikalyan.mp.gov.in. Children pursuing graduation or professional courses such as engineering, medical, law, management or polytechnic in a government or recognised private college can receive full tuition fee reimbursement if their parent is an active Sambal enrolee.

Electricity subsidy is the most widely used Sambal benefit in terms of number of households reached. BPL families registered under the scheme receive the first 200 units of electricity free every month, with the zero-billing applied automatically once the Sambal registration ID is successfully mapped to the household's electricity consumer account with the local DISCOM.

items.title: Free electricity
items.sub: BPL Sambal households get the first 200 units free each month once the registration is mapped to the DISCOM consumer account.

items.title: Education support
items.sub: Children get full tuition reimbursement for graduation or professional courses via the Medhavi Kalyan scheme at medhavikalyan.mp.gov.in.

items.title: Farm and housing aid
items.sub: Registered farmers get free improved seed kits each season. SECC-listed families get priority on the PM Awas Gramin housing list.

extra_sections.heading: Filing Claims Online and Offline
content: Online claims can be filed by logging into sambal.mp.gov.in with the registered mobile number and Samagra ID, then navigating to the 'Benefit Application' section. The applicant selects the relevant benefit type, fills in event details, uploads supporting documents in PDF or JPEG format, and submits to receive a claim reference number for tracking.

Offline claims can be filed at the Gram Panchayat Secretary's office in rural areas or the Ward Officer's office in urban areas. The official enters the claim details into the Sambal portal on the beneficiary's behalf after checking documents, which is especially helpful for older or less tech-savvy workers who cannot navigate the portal independently.

extra_sections.heading: If a Claim Is Delayed or Rejected
content: If a claim is rejected, the portal's beneficiary dashboard displays the rejection reason along with a resubmission option. Common reasons include an inactive Sambal registration at the time of the event, incomplete or illegible document scans, bank account mismatch with the Aadhaar-seeded account, or the worker being found under ESIC coverage at the time of the incident.

Workers with grievances that remain unresolved at the Panchayat or Block level can escalate by calling the CM Helpline at 181 (toll-free, 24x7), which handles queries across all MP government schemes. The dedicated Sambal helpline at 0755-2573036 and 0755-2573046 connects to the Welfare Board office directly, and written complaints can be emailed to commlab@nic.in.

extra_sections.title: Why a Claim Gets Rejected
extra_sections.content:
The most common reasons are an inactive Sambal registration at the time of the event, or document scans that are incomplete or illegible.

Others include a bank account that does not match the Aadhaar-seeded account, or the worker being found under ESIC cover at the time. The portal shows the reason and a resubmit option.

extra_sections.heading: Checking Status and Downloading the Card
content: Status of both registration and individual claims can be checked any time on sambal.mp.gov.in by clicking 'Avedan ki sthiti' and entering the Samagra ID. The dashboard shows whether the registration is active, pending Panchayat verification, or suspended, and also displays transaction ID and payment date for any disbursed claim.

The Sambal Card can be downloaded at any time from sambal.mp.gov.in by logging in with the registered mobile number, navigating to 'Sambal Card Download' and entering the Samagra ID. The downloaded PDF carries a QR code that can be scanned by government officers to instantly verify the beneficiary's registration status and benefit history.

extra_sections.heading: Sambal Card Download and Status Check

items.title: Download the Sambal Card
items.sub: Log in at sambal.mp.gov.in with your registered mobile number, click Sambal Card Download, and enter your Samagra ID. The PDF carries a QR code for instant verification.

items.title: Check application status
items.sub: Click Avedan ki sthiti on the portal and enter your Samagra ID to see if registration is active, pending verification, or suspended.

items.title: Track a claim payment
items.sub: The dashboard shows the transaction ID and payment date for any disbursed claim against your Samagra ID.

items.title: Fix card details
items.sub: Name, address, bank, or mobile changes must be corrected first on samagra.gov.in. Updates reflect in the Sambal portal within 24 to 48 hours.

extra_sections.heading: Updating Details and Grievances
content: Any change in name, address, bank account or mobile number must be corrected first on samagra.gov.in, since the Sambal portal draws all personal data from the Samagra database and does not maintain a separate edit interface. Corrections on Samagra typically reflect in the Sambal portal within 24 to 48 hours without requiring a separate update request.

The nominee registered on the Sambal Card is the primary recipient for accidental and natural death benefits. If the nominee changes due to marriage, death, or other circumstances, the beneficiary must update the nominee details on the Sambal portal by logging in and editing the profile section, followed by Aadhaar-based OTP verification.

faqs.question: What is the Sambal Card in Madhya Pradesh?
faqs.answer: The Sambal Card is a beneficiary identity document issued after registration under Mukhyamantri Jan Kalyan (Sambal) Yojana. It links the worker's Samagra ID, Aadhaar, nominee details and bank account, and must be produced when filing any benefit claim such as accidental death cover, maternity assistance or funeral aid.

faqs.question: What is the accidental death benefit under Sambal Yojana MP?
faqs.answer: The accidental death benefit is Rs 4,00,000, paid as a lump sum via DBT to the registered nominee's bank account within 60 days of a complete claim. Natural or general death carries a separate benefit of Rs 2,00,000 for the family.

faqs.question: How do I register for Sambal Yojana MP online?
faqs.answer: Visit sambal.mp.gov.in, click on the registration link, enter your Samagra family ID and individual member ID, fill in occupation and bank account details, upload your Aadhaar, BPL card, bank passbook and photo, then submit. The Gram Panchayat or Ward Office verifies the application within 15 to 30 days and issues the Sambal Card.

faqs.question: Is Samagra ID mandatory for Sambal Yojana registration?
faqs.answer: Yes, Samagra ID is compulsory and the Sambal portal cannot be used without it. Register your family at samagra.gov.in or through the Gram Panchayat to get a 9-digit family ID before starting the Sambal application.

faqs.question: What is the maternity benefit under Sambal Yojana and how do I apply?
faqs.answer: Registered women workers receive Rs 16,000 in maternity assistance through the linked Mukhyamantri Shramik Seva Prasuti Sahayata Yojna. Apply at the nearest public health centre or Block Family Welfare Department office at least six weeks before the expected delivery date, and the amount is paid in installments via DBT.

faqs.question: How do I claim the funeral assistance of Rs 5,000?
faqs.answer: Visit your nearest Gram Panchayat or Ward Office with the death certificate and the worker's Sambal Card number. The Panchayat Secretary uploads the claim on the Sambal portal on your behalf, and the Rs 5,000 is typically processed within 48 hours as immediate last-rites relief.

faqs.question: Does Sambal Yojana cover electricity bills for workers?
faqs.answer:
Yes. BPL households registered under Sambal receive the first 200 units of electricity free every month.

The zero-unit billing is applied automatically once the Sambal registration ID is mapped to the household's electricity consumer account by the local DISCOM office.

faqs.question: How do I check my Sambal registration or claim payment status?
faqs.answer: Go to sambal.mp.gov.in and click on 'Avedan ki sthiti' (Application Status), then enter your Samagra ID. The portal shows whether registration is active, pending or approved, and displays the transaction ID and disbursement date for any completed claim payment.

faqs.question: What are the disability benefits under Sambal Yojana MP?
faqs.answer:
Permanent disability caused by an accident qualifies the worker for Rs 2,00,000. Partial permanent disability carries Rs 1,00,000.

A disability certificate from a government hospital specifying the nature and degree of disability must be submitted along with the Sambal Card and Aadhaar to process the claim.

faqs.question: Can workers covered under ESIC or EPF apply for Sambal Yojana?
faqs.answer: No. Workers already receiving ESIC or EPF coverage are not eligible for Sambal Yojana, as they are considered organised-sector employees with existing formal social security. Sambal is exclusively for workers in the unorganised informal economy.

faqs.question: How does Sambal Yojana support children's higher education?
faqs.answer: Children of Sambal-enrolled workers can apply for full tuition fee reimbursement through the Mukhyamantri Medhavi Vidyarthi Kalyan Yojana at medhavikalyan.mp.gov.in. The scheme covers graduation, engineering, medical, law, management and polytechnic programmes in government and recognised private institutions.

faqs.question: What is Naya Savera Yojana and is it the same as Sambal Yojana?
faqs.answer:
Yes, they are the same scheme. Sambal Yojana was renamed Naya Savera Yojana by the Congress government in 2018 and then restored as Mukhyamantri Jan Kalyan (Sambal 2.0) Yojana after BJP returned to power in 2020.

Workers registered under Naya Savera were asked to re-register under Sambal 2.0 on the same portal.
